caseno: Civil Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 1500 of 2013.
lawyer:
Mr. Md. Abdus Salam Mondal, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Syed Mahbubar Rahman Advocate-on-Record --------- For the Petitioners. 
Mr. Md. Shamsul Hoque, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Haridas Paul, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent No. 1. 
Respondents Nos.2-25:----- Not represented.
parties:
Hamed Kazi Being Dead His Heirs: 1(A) Mohammad Kazi And Others
Vs.
Jitendra Nath Halder
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali, J:-This civil petition for leave to appeal arises out of the judgement and order dated 21.11.2012 passed by a Single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.4915 of 2004 discharging the Rule.

<u>2. The predecessors of the petitioners 1(a)-1(f) and others as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No.84 of 2000 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Nazirpur, Pirojpur against respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and other co-sharers in the suit property for a declaration that the judgement and decree dated 20.10.2000 in Title Suit No.217 of 1983 of the Court of Assistant Judge, Nazirpur was obtained collusively and fraudulently and not enforceable upon them and also for a separate saham in respect of their property. They contended, inter alia, that the suit property originally belonged to C.S recorded owners, namely Keduram Haider, Chutu Halder and Kashinath Halder, sons of Rain Krishna Halder in eight annas share and the remaining eight annas share was owned and possessed by their paternal uncle Dwarika Nath Halder. Kashinath Haider died issueless leaving wife Biddya Sundari, who inherited his share and Dwarika Nath Haider also died unmarried and his share devolved upon his two nephews, Keduram and Chutu Halder in equal share and thus Chutu Halder got 2 annas 13 gandas by inheritance in the paternal property and 4 annas from his uncle Dwarika Nath and thereafter Chutu Haider died leaving only son Amaresh Haider. While Amaresh Haider owned and possessed 5.09 acres of land, on 26.02.1953 he transferred 44 decimals to Afzal Kazi and Hamed Kazi and before that on 12.05.1952 Amaresh transferred 17 decimals of land to Rafiz Uddin Kazi and Hamed Kazi though Hamed Kazi paid the entire consideration money and was in possession of the said property, but he got the sale deed registered in Benami of one Asman Khan for the reasons best known to him. Amaresh again on 02.04.1956 transferred 1.00 acre of land to Hamed Kazi and Rafiz Uddin Kazi. Keduram Haider died leaving three sons, namely Shasti Haider, Ambika Haider and Jageshwar Haider who inherited their father's property and while they had been owning and possessing, they along with the aforesaid Biddya Sundari and Amaresh Haider transferred 2.69 acres of land to Jagesh Chandra Mondal, Rajendra Nath Mondal and Brajendra Nath Mondal. Thereafter, one of the purchasers Brajendra Nath Mondal died leaving two sons, Subhas and Ashim Mondal, who sold 27 decimals of land to Hamed Kazi on 09.02.1979 and put him into possession. While he had been owning and possessing his share in the suit property Rafizuddin Kazi died leaving wife Golapi Bibi, three sons, namely Jalal. Alal and Afzal and 3 daughters, namely Mohna, Zohra and Sahera to inherit his 582decimals out of which Sahera got 6 decimals which she transferred to petitioner No.2 by way of Heba. As such, the petitioners own and possess the `B' schedule land of the suit property described in the plaint, the extent of which is 1.88 acres. They use some portion as homestead, some portion for gardening and some portion for cultivation producing different crops. On 15.07.2000 opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 disclosed that they have obtained the homestead portion of the suit land by virtue of a decree obtained in Title Suit No.217 of 1983 from the Court of the Assistant Judge, Nazirpur, Pirojpur and when confirmed about the said disclosure from the Court, the original petitioner forthwith applied for certified copy of the judgement and decree on 20.07.2000 and obtained the same on 14.08.2000 and thereafter filed the instant suit.</u>

3. The principal defendant —respondent Nos. 1 and 2 herein contested the suit by filing separate written statements refuting all the material allegations as unfolded in the plaint contending in a nutshell that previously the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 filed a suit for partition in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Nazirpur, Pirojpur being Title Suit No.217 of 1983 against respondent No.2 and others and thereafter the suit was dismissed on contest against which the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No.126 of 1986 before the District Judge, Pirojpur and upon hearing the parties the appeal was allowed setting aside the judgement and decree and sending the suit on remand to the trial Court. After remand the suit was decreed, against which the principal defendant-respondent No.2 preferred Title Appeal No.15 of 1990 before the District Judge, who on hearing the parties allowed the appeal and again remanded the suit to the trial Court. At that stage respondent No.1 compromised the suit with respondent No.2, the suit was decreed on the basis of solenama, and as such the present Title Suit No.84 of 2000 is not maintainable.

4. After hearing the parties and considering the materials on record the Assistant Judge by his judgement and decree dated 23.04.2003 decreed the suit.

5. Against the aforesaid judgement and decree the defendant-respondent No.1 preferred Title Appeal No. 55 of 2003 before the District Judge, Pirojpur. The appeal was transferred to the Court of Joint District Judge, Second Court, Perojpur, who after hearing the parties allowed the appeal setting aside the judgement and decree of the trial Court by his judgement and decree dated 02.01.2004.

6. Being aggrieved, the plaintiff filed Civil Revision No.4915 of 2004 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which upon hearing the parties was discharged. Hence, the heirs of the plaintiff arc now before us having filed the instant civil petition for leave to appeal.

<u>7. Mr. Md. Abdus Salam Mondal, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that the Assistant Judge on careful consideration and meticulous analysis of the evidence, both oral and documentary, was pleased to decree the suit, but on appeal therefrom at the instance of the defendant-respondent Nos.1 and 2 the appellate Court erroneousiy allowed the appeal setting aside the judgement and decree on point of limitation, court fees and question of maintainability and the High Court Division on hearing the civil revision without entering into the merits of the case erroneously discharged the Rule, which is not sustainable in law. He further submitted that the appellate Court manifestly erred in law in allowing the appeal without proper reasoning and the High Court Division also committed error in discharging the Rule merely as barred by estoppel under section 115 of the Evidence Act though the law does not say so, because of the fact that the compromise decree was secretly made and obtained at a time when the suit came back on remand for the second time and the compromise was made between only the plaintiff and defendant No.1 of Title Suit No.217 of 1983 and no other defendants were aware of the same. He also submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in discharging the Rule without taking proper notice of the principle of estoppel as embodied in section 115 of the Evidence Act as it is a rule of evidence by which a person is not allowed to allege and prove a thing under certain circumstances, but it is well settled that before a party could be barred by the principle to estoppel, waiver and acquiescence it must be established that the opposite party respondent acted bona fide on the clear, definite and unambiguous representation made by their adversary and that the opposite party respondents have altered their position in pursuance thereof. Even a mere gratuitous indulgence shown to a party in not enforcing its legal right for the time being cannot constitute estoppel or waiver and as such the impugned judgement and order is not sustainable in law. He submitted that the plaintiff-respondent No.1 of Title Suit No.217 of 1983(partition), i.e. defendant-respondent Nos. 1 and 2 of Title Suit No.84 of 2000 after remand for the second time made a compromise decree secretly which is tantamount to an ex parte decree against the plaintiffs-petitioners and other defendants and by compromise decree practicing fraud they tried to grab the petitioner's property and from the knowledge of the aforesaid compromise decree they filed the instant suit within statutory period, and upon hearing the trial Court decreed the suit. On the other hand, the appellate Court as well as High Court Division erroneously and arbitrarily dismissed the suit without proper analysis of the evidence as well as relevant laws. He submitted that the appellate Court as well as the High Court Division in passing the judgement totally failed to consider the ownership and possession of the petitioners in the suit property 1.88 acres which they have been owning and possessing and residing in some portion thereof by constructing houses for more than 12 years by valid purchase. The learned Advocate lastly submitted that the High Court Division arrived at an abrupt decision to discharge the Rule upholding the order of the appellate Court that the suit is barred by estoppel without proper appreciation of the relevant law, as such the impugned judgement and order is not sustainable in law.</u>

8. Mr. Shamsul Hoque, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent made submissions in support of the impugned judgement and order of the High Court Division.

9. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the impugned judgement of the High Court Division and other connected papers on record.

<u>10. It appears from the evidence and materials on record that in the instant suit the plaintiffs sought a declaration that the judgement and decree dated 20.10.2000 in Title Suit No. 217 of 1983 was obtained collusively and fraudulently. The earlier suit was one for partition and was ultimately decreed on the basis of a solenama and the plaintiffs of the instant suit contested the earlier suit and also prayed for saham. We find from the order sheet of earlier partition suit that defendant Nos. 9 to 13 filed an application praying for saham but that application was rejected because the applicants did not sign the application, but the trial Court noted that the earlier suit was decreed giving more than the due share to the defendants, who were party to the solenama. The appellate Court, on the other hand, noted that the solenama decree was passed in the earlier suit on 13.10.1997 and after that defendant Nos. 9 to 13 of that suit, who are the plaintiffs in the present suit filed an application praying for saham which was rejected on 01.03.1998. Their application for saham was filed again and was again rejected on 15.04.1998 and the decree was made final upon receipt of the Advocate Commissioner's report. The appellate Court observed that there was neither any revision filed against the rejection of the application for saham nor any appeal filed against the preliminary or final decree. The appellate Court concluded that the plaintiffs could not prove that the earlier suit was decreed without their knowledge and consent. The appellate Court pointed out that P.W. 1 admitted in his cross-examination that they went into possession in accordance with the final decree of Title Suit No. 217 of 1983.</u>

11. The High Court Division also noted that the lower court record of Title Suit No. 217 of 1983 clearly reflected that the present petitioners contested throughout the proceedings and thereafter abstained from making any objection against the Advocate Commissioner's report and thereby they are barred by estoppel from making any objection against the same when the final decree was withdrawn on 10.10.1999 and after that through application before the same Court they have withdrawn their papers.

12. Perusal of the judgement of the appellate Court shows that there was elaborate discussion of all the material points raised, and the judgement and decree of the trial Court was reversed upon proper scrutiny of the evidence and materials on record. In our view the High Court Division has rightly upheld the judgement and decree of the appellate Court and has given adequate reasons for doing so.

13. In view of the above discussion we do not find any illegality or impropriety in the impugned judgement and the same does not call for any interference. Accordingly, the civil petition for leave to appeal is dismissed.

End.
